::: {.lead}
Today there are no new ideas. You revise Lectures 1–10 by solving one game
problem from each part of the course: vectors, the two products, distance
and projection, trigonometry, matrices and transformations. Do each activity
alone. The results of the activities are at the end of this worksheet: try
first, then compare.
:::

## Recall

![Lectures 1–10 in six parts.](images/course-map.png){width=88%}

- **Vectors (Lectures 1–2):** a step is B − A; length |v| = √(x² + y²);
  unit vector v ÷ |v|; velocity = speed × unit direction.
- **Two products (Lectures 3–4):** a · b = a~x~ b~x~ + a~y~ b~y~ (in front or
  behind); 2D a × b = a~x~ b~y~ − a~y~ b~x~ (left or right).
- **Distance and projection (Lecture 5):** distance |B − A|; along = v · û.
- **Trigonometry (Lectures 6–7):** the direction at θ is (cos θ, sin θ);
  atan2(y, x) gives the angle of a vector.
- **Matrices (Lecture 8):** rows times columns; I changes nothing; the
  inverse undoes.
- **Transformations (Lectures 9–10):** T, S, R; about a pivot: −C,
  transform, +C; M = T × R × S; points w = 1, directions w = 0.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="14|(1, 0)"}
How long is (6, 8)?
:   10

    Why: √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10, not 6 + 8.

What is (2, 3) · (−3, 2)?
:   0

    Why: −6 + 6 = 0: the vectors are perpendicular.

What is R(90°) × (1, 0)?
:   (0, 1)

    Why: (−y, x) = (0, 1).
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · A ship's trip

A ship sails from (−2, 3) to (4, −5) at 2 units per second.

![Adding vectors head to tail.](../week-02/images/vector-add.png){width=78%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Step, length, time · 10 min"}
1. Find the step from start to end and its length.
2. Find the unit direction and the velocity at 2 units per second.
3. How long does the trip take?

*Your product:* the step, its length, the unit direction, the velocity and
the time.

::: {.check}
Step (6, −8); length √(36 + 64) = 10; unit direction (0.6, −0.8); velocity
2 × (0.6, −0.8) = (1.2, −1.6); time 10 ÷ 2 = 5 seconds.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Vectors"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(6, 8)|7 s"}
Normalize (0, −4).
:   (0, −1)

    Why: its length is 4; (0 ÷ 4, −4 ÷ 4).

A drone flies (6, 8) at 5 units per second. Its velocity?
:   (3, 4)

    Why: unit direction (0.6, 0.8) × 5.

A trip of 10 units at 2 units per second takes…
:   5 s

    Why: time = distance ÷ speed.
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · The guard and the turret

A guard looks along f = (1, 0). Three players stand at d = (3, 4), (−3, 4)
and (2, −1) from the guard.

![The sign of the dot product.](../week-02/images/dot-sign.png){width=78%}

{{< sim file="../week-02/sims/dot-lab.html" poster="../week-02/sims/dot-lab.png" title="Dot Lab: two vectors, one number" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Front, back, left, right · 12 min"}
1. For each player, compute f · d. In front or behind?
2. For each player, compute the 2D cross product f × d. Left or right?
3. Check one player in **Dot Lab**.

*Your product:* a table with three rows: d, f · d, front or behind, f × d,
left or right.

::: {.check}
(3, 4): f · d = 3, in front; f × d = 4, left. (−3, 4): −3, behind; 4, left.
(2, −1): 2, in front; −1, right.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Two products"}
The guard looks along f = (1, 0). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="in front|right"}
A player at d = (−3, 4). In front or behind?
:   behind

    Why: f · d = −3 is negative.

A player at d = (2, −1). Left or right?
:   to the right

    Why: f × d = 1 × (−1) − 0 × 2 = −1: negative.

What is (1, 0, 0) × (0, 1, 0)?
:   (0, 0, 1)

    Why: the x-axis × the y-axis gives the z-axis.
:::
:::

## Activity 3 · The nearest enemy and the beam

A tower stands at (0, 0). Enemies are at (3, 4), (−5, 1) and (2, −2). A beam
from the tower goes along û = (0.6, 0.8).

![The car's shadow on the road: the projection.](../week-03/images/projection.png){width=78%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 3 · Nearest and along · 10 min"}
1. Which enemy is nearest? Compare the squares.
2. How far along the beam is each enemy (v · û)?
3. Which enemy is behind the tower, seen from the beam?

*Your product:* three squares, three "along" values and one answer.

::: {.check}
Squares 25, 26, 8: (2, −2) is nearest. Along: (3, 4): 1.8 + 3.2 = 5;
(−5, 1): −3 + 0.8 = −2.2; (2, −2): 1.2 − 1.6 = −0.4. (−5, 1) and (2, −2) give a
negative value: both are behind the start of the beam.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Distance and projection"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(3, 4)|7"}
Which enemy is nearest to (0, 0): (3, 4), (−5, 1) or (2, −2)?
:   (2, −2)

    Why: its square 4 + 4 = 8 is the smallest.

The distance between (1, 1) and (4, 5).
:   5

    Why: (3, 4) has the length 5.

v = (3, −2) hits a floor with the normal (0, 1). The slide?
:   (3, 0)

    Why: remove the part into the floor: (3, −2) − (−2)(0, 1).
:::
:::

## Activity 4 · Aim and fire

A cannon fires at 60° with the speed 20 (cos 60° = 0.5, sin 60° = 0.87). A
turret faces 350° and must aim at an enemy at (−4, 4).

![The unit circle.](../week-04/images/unit-circle.png){width=78%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 4 · Angles · 12 min"}
1. Find the velocity of the cannon ball.
2. Find the angle of the enemy with atan2(4, −4).
3. The turret faces 350° and must face 10°. What is the short turn?

*Your product:* one velocity, one angle and one turn.

::: {.check}
Velocity 20 × (0.5, 0.87) = (10, 17.4). atan2(4, −4) = 135° (quadrant II).
Short turn: 10° − 350° = −340°; + 360° = +20°, to the left.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Angles"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(17.4, 10)|45°"}
A cannon fires at 60° with the speed 20. The velocity?
:   (10, 17.4)

    Why: 20 × (cos 60°, sin 60°).

Which angle does atan2(−3, −3) give?
:   −135°

    Why: both parts negative: quadrant III.

Facing 350°, target 10°. The short turn?
:   +20°

    Why: −340° + 360°.
:::
:::

## Activity 5 · Spells and their undo

Two spells: A has the rows (1, 2) and (0, 1); B has the rows (3, 0) and
(1, 1). Grow has the rows (2, 0) and (0, 2).

![A matrix times a vector.](../week-05/images/matrix-vector.png){width=78%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 5 · Matrices · 10 min"}
1. Compute AB and BA. Are they equal?
2. Compute A × (1, 1).
3. Which matrix undoes Grow? Check it on (3, 2).

*Your product:* two matrices, one point and one inverse with its check.

::: {.check}
AB = rows (5, 2) and (1, 1). BA = rows (3, 6) and (1, 3). Not equal: the order
matters. A × (1, 1) = (3, 1). Shrink, rows (0.5, 0) and (0, 0.5): Grow sends
(3, 2) to (6, 4), and Shrink brings it back to (3, 2).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Matrices"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="rows (3, 0), (0, 1)|(4, 6)"}
Rows (1, 2), (0, 1) times rows (3, 0), (1, 1).
:   rows (5, 2), (1, 1)

    Why: row 1 · columns: 3 + 2 = 5, 0 + 2 = 2; row 2: 1, 1.

Rows (1, 2), (3, 4) times (1, 1).
:   (3, 7)

    Why: 1 + 2 = 3 and 3 + 4 = 7.

Which matrix undoes Grow, rows (2, 0), (0, 2)?
:   rows (0.5, 0), (0, 0.5)

    Why: Grow doubles; halving undoes it.
:::
:::

## Activity 6 · One matrix for the move

A flag sits at (1, 0) in its own space. It is turned by 180° and moved by
(2, 3). A door turns about its hinge (1, 1).

![The TRS matrix.](../week-07/images/trs-chain.png){width=78%}

{{< sim file="../week-07/sims/matrix-chain.html" poster="../week-07/sims/matrix-chain.png" title="Matrix Chain: M = T × R × S" height="820" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 6 · Transformations · 12 min"}
1. Write M = T(2, 3) × R(180°) as a 3 × 3 matrix. Where does the flag
   (1, 0, 1) go? Check in **Matrix Chain**.
2. Where does the direction (1, 0, 0) go with M?
3. Rotate the door handle (2, 0) by 90° about the hinge (1, 1).

*Your product:* one matrix and three results.

::: {.check}
M = rows (−1, 0, 2), (0, −1, 3), (0, 0, 1). The flag goes to (1, 3). The
direction goes to (−1, 0): only turned. The handle: (2, 0) − (1, 1) =
(1, −1); R(90°) gives (1, 1); + (1, 1) = (2, 2).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · Transformations"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(0, 2)|(4, 4)"}
Rotate (2, 0) by 90° about the pivot (1, 1).
:   (2, 2)

    Why: (1, −1) → (1, 1); + (1, 1).

Apply T(−1, 2) to (4, 4, 1).
:   (3, 6, 1)

    Why: (4 − 1, 4 + 2, 1).

A tank has a yaw of 90°. Its forward vector?
:   (1, 0, 0)

    Why: (sin 90°, 0, cos 90°).
:::
:::

## Case study: Island Quest

*Island Quest* is a made-up revision game. A boat sails around six islands,
one for each part of Lectures 1–10, and on each island the player solves one
problem from a game: a drone's flight, a guard's view, a ball on a floor, a
cannon's aim, a spell and its undo, and a flag moved by one matrix. The Game
challenge of the interactive page asks these questions.

{{< sim file="sims/island-quest.html" poster="sims/island-quest.png" title="Island Quest: one problem on each island" kind="game" height="640" >}}

## Exercises

1. A ship sails from (1, −1) to (4, 3). Find the step, its length and the
   unit direction.
2. A guard looks along (0, 1). Is a player at d = (2, −3) in front or behind?
   Left or right?
3. Enemies at (6, 8) and (−7, 1) from a tower. Which is nearer?
4. A ball flies at 30° with the speed 4 (cos 30° = 0.87, sin 30° = 0.5).
   Find its velocity.
5. Facing 20°, target 340°. Find the short turn.
6. Compute rows (2, 0), (1, 1) times (3, 4).
7. Rotate (3, 1) by 180° about the pivot (1, 1).
8. M = T(1, 2) × R(90°). Where does the point (2, 0, 1) go?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. (3, 4); 5; (0.6, 0.8).
2. f · d = −3: behind. f × d = 0 × (−3) − 1 × 2 = −2: to the right.
3. Squares 100 and 50: (−7, 1) is nearer.
4. (3.48, 2).
5. 340° − 20° = 320°; − 360° = −40°: 40° to the right.
6. (6, 7).
7. (3, 1) − (1, 1) = (2, 0); R(180°) gives (−2, 0); + (1, 1) = (−1, 1).
8. R(90°) × (2, 0) = (0, 2); + (1, 2) = (1, 4).
:::
